name: kensio
description: Claude Code skills from Kensio Software — reusable, opinionated ways of working, packaged as installable plugins.

plugins.name: isolated-testing-style
plugins.description: An opinionated testing style: start from given/when/then, use real collaborators through simulation instead of stubs, take isolation from randomised data instead of shared setup and teardown, and assert behaviour instead of call counts.

plugins.name: yulin-aws-simulation
plugins.description: How to test AWS code well with the @kensio/yulin in-process simulator: using it directly instead of building a harness around it, driving tests, local dev and production from one synthesized CDK template, intercepting SDK clients, controlling simulated time, and handling what the simulator refuses.

plugins.name: part-factory-test-data
plugins.description: How to build test data with @kensio/part-factory: keeping in the factory everything a test does not care about, passing dependencies at call time so factories stay independent and shareable, and choosing between its static, dynamic, variant and mapped factories.

plugins.name: technical-prose-style
plugins.description: Plain technical prose for docs, READMEs, comments and commit messages: five measured sentence shapes to remove, the style rules that turn out not to matter, and a script that scores prose against Django and Go documentation.

plugins.name: skill-template
plugins.description: A copy-and-edit starting point for writing a new Claude Code skill, covering SKILL.md frontmatter, description wording, and progressive disclosure.
